newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Vietnam-Kuwait signs '97/98 diesel/jet fuel deal.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam-Kuwait signs '97/98 diesel/jet fuel deal.

text.p: State-owned Vietnam National Petroleum Import-Export Corp (Petrolimex) has signed a term contract to buy diesel and jet fuel from state-owned Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) for deliveries in 1997 and 1998, an industry source said on Friday.
Under the contract, which was signed on Wednesday, Petrolimex will import 670,000 tonnes of 1.0-percent sulphur diesel and 140,000 tonnes of jet fuel per year.
In its previous contract for 1996, Petrolimex imported 500,000 tonnes of diesel and 80,000 tonnes of jet fuel from KPC.

The source said the diesel price was about five cents more than the price agreed for the last six months of the 1996 contract which was 10 cents per barrel premium to Singapore spot quotes, on a free-on-board (fob) Singapore basis.

In the previous deal, prices on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to Ho Chi Minh City were more than 80 cents premium to Singapore spot quotes, and c-and-f Danang premiums were around 95 cents a barrel.

The source said jet fuel prices for the new contract remained around the same price as in the last six months of the 1996 contract which were 20 cents per barrel above Singapore spot quotes, fob Singapore.
He said there would be nine deliveries per year, with four cargoes of diesel and jet fuel per delivery.
Each delivery would be made every 36 days and would include three c-and-f cargoes, to Ho Chi Minh City, Danang and Hongai, and one fob Singapore cargo.
The source said some of the jet fuel imports are reexported to Cambodia, while the balance is sold as kerosene to the domestic market and the Vietnamese army.
The source also said that Petrolimex would not renew its term contract with Japan's Marubeni International Petroleum Co (Mipco), a unit of Japan's Marubeni Corp.
Petrolimex entered into a term deal with Mipco in March for deliveries of 180,000-200,000 tonnes of diesel between April and December 1996.
